criteria.description: Correctly justifies via known functional form + few unknown constants.

solutions.fullSolution: Parameter estimation: the physics functional form (Newton-Euler/Euler-Lagrange) is known, only specific constants (masses, inertias) are unknown. A handful of trials can pin down few physical constants precisely; full regression would need to learn the entire functional form from scratch, needing far more data.

criteria.description: Correctly reframes the loss in terms of a residual target delta_t.
Correctly explains why this is an easier learning problem.

solutions.fullSolution: Define delta_t = x_t - f_M(x_{t-1},u_{t-1}). Then L(theta) = sum_t ||delta_t - f_theta(x_{t-1},u_{t-1})||^2, an ordinary regression with target delta_t. If f_M is reasonable, delta_t is small and structurally simple (e.g. a smooth aerodynamic correction), so f_theta only needs to learn a small correction rather than the full dynamics from scratch, easier to fit from limited data.

criteria.description: Correctly contrasts autoregression's fixed window vs recurrent's implicit latent summary.
Correctly explains state-space models' explicit state commitment.

solutions.fullSolution: Autoregression uses a fixed explicit window of past observations directly, no learned latent summary. A generic recurrent model learns an implicit latent summary h_t with no particular structural assumption. A state-space model is also recurrent but explicitly commits the latent variable to be a genuine system state x_t, jointly training decoding g and dynamics f, giving an interpretable representation rather than an arbitrary hidden state.
